headline: Florida Plants 15,000 Native Milkweeds to Save Monarchs
meta_description: Florida is converting roadside land into monarch butterfly habitat by planting native milkweeds, with researchers aiming to plant up to 15,000 by 2029.

body:
Florida is converting roadside land into monarch butterfly habitat, with researchers planting up to 15,000 native milkweeds through 2029. The effort is already showing results—monarchs have begun using some of the newly planted vegetation.

The initiative addresses a critical need for the iconic species. Milkweed is the only plant monarch caterpillars eat, making it essential to their survival. By transforming underused roadside areas into native plant zones, Florida is creating much-needed food sources along migration routes.

The project represents a practical approach to conservation, using existing land while supporting both wildlife and the natural landscape. As the planting effort continues toward 2029, researchers will be watching to see how the expanding network of native plants supports monarch populations.
